claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you applying for Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child named Alex that you're inquiring about.

To help assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation:

**Are you and Alex both living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. Alex doesn't actually live with me though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Can you tell me more about where Alex lives and what the living arrangements are? For example, does Alex live with another parent, a guardian, or in another country?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with my ex-partner. I don't live with them, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards Alex's upkeep regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. That helps me understand the situation better.

**Are you a British citizen or do you have settled status in the UK? Alternatively, are you a national of an EEA country or Switzerland?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Does Alex's other parent (your ex-partner) currently claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are you aware of whether they do?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, my ex-partner doesn't claim Child Benefit for Alex. They're not getting it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you responsible for Alex financially - meaning do you provide for Alex's essential needs such as food, accommodation, and clothing? Or is Alex primarily supported by their other parent or another person?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute financially. I help pay for things Alex needs - like clothes, food, that sort of thing. I send money regularly to help with their upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I have a few more questions to complete the picture.

**Does Alex live with you for a significant amount of time, such as staying with you regularly or on a shared custody arrangement? Or is the contact mainly financial support without Alex living at your address?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't stay with me. They live full-time with my ex-partner. I just provide the financial support to help with their needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**What is your current residential status in the UK? For example, are you settled in the UK permanently, or do you have any visa or other immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so I'm settled here permanently in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the key details:

- You are a British citizen settled permanently in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old
- Alex lives full-time with your ex-partner
- You provide regular financial support towards Alex's upkeep
- You do not have Alex living with you
- Your ex-partner does not claim Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of Your Eligibility for Child Benefit:**

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why?**
The main reason is that while you do provide financial support towards Alex's upkeep, Child Benefit requires that the child lives with you as part of your household. Since Alex lives full-time with your ex-partner and not with you, you don't meet the residency requirement for eligibility.

**What might help?**
Your ex-partner could potentially claim Child Benefit for Alex if they meet the other eligibility requirements. Even though they currently don't claim it, they may be able to do so.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex were to move in with you), please don't hesitate to reach out.
